Based on my research, here's the answer to your question:

**The Bacchanal of the Andrians** was created by **Titian** (Tiziano Vecellio), a Venetian Renaissance painter. Titian died in **Venice** (specifically in the Cannaregio district) on August 27, 1576.

**Roncalli** refers to **Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli**, who later became **Pope John XXIII**. In 1953, he was appointed as the **Patriarch of Venice**, making Venice his home until 1958.

**Why Roncalli left Venice:**
He left Venice when he was **summoned to Rome for the papal conclave** following the death of Pope Pius XII on October 9, 1958. On **October 28, 1958**, Roncalli was elected as Pope John XXIII. Although he had intended for Venice to be his final earthly home, the call to become Pope required him to return to Rome.

This is quite an interesting historical coincidence - the artist who created The Bacchanal of the Andrians died in Venice nearly 382 years before Roncalli departed the same city to become the Pope.
